To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the strength of sexual selection for two sexual signals (tail length, ventral coloration) differs between two populations, sexes and age groups of the barn swallow.

(1) the barn swallow populations from Czech Republic differ from those from Romania in selection on tail and ventral color, and (2) the barn swallow population in Romania differs from that in Czech Republic in tail and ventral colouration.

(i) the intensity and targets of selection on sexual signals differ between the Czech and Romanian barn swallow populations; (ii) the intensity of selection on tail length differs between age classes and sexes; and (iii) ventral coloration varies between sexes, age classes, and populations.
In summary, our research is concerned with

variation in sexual selection on tail length and ventrally located sexual characters in two Central and East Europe populations of the barn swallows, and the relationship between sexual selection and phenotypic variation in these traits.
the effects of population differences in selection on multiple sexual signals, and it provides a better understanding of the mechanisms of sexual selection and phenotypic divergence in this species.
the variation in selection for multiple sexual traits across different populations, and the relationship between sexual selection and sexual characters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the barn swallow shows population differences in the intensity and targets of selection on multiple sexual signals, and these differences are related to the local conditions.
selection on tail size and ventral color variation is population‐specific and may be related to differences in breeding conditions and/or sexual dimorphism.

the differences in selection on multiple sexual signals between the Czech and Romanian populations of the barn swallows might be due to differences in breeding conditions, but also due to differences in the intensity of sexual selection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sexual selection on multiple sexual signals is not uniform across populations.
the intensity of selection on tail length and ventrual coloration varies between populations, sexes and age classes.
sexual selection on multiple characters may vary among populations and that these differences may be related to the variation in breeding conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the strength and direction of sexual selection can differ among populations and age classes.
the intensity and targets of selection may differ between populations, and this difference may depend on the breeding conditions and the age of the birds.
